investigation.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-26T12:27:14–48Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity is established, zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed upstream that the production-api proxies agent-creation requests to at /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every attempt. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agent checks, the shared upstream failure cascaded identically across remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 717 minutes old, which is 2.39x the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to any broader website or infrastructure outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 717 minutes (approximately 12 hours). The expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot's source field confirms it is produced by github-actions, meaning the upstream workflow — not the eval runner or the website serving layer — is the component that has stalled or failed. This is an eval-detected operational gap in the snapshot publishing pipeline, not a user-facing website outage.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot has not completed a successful run in over 717 minutes. This could be due to a workflow being disabled, a scheduling gap, a runner quota exhaustion, a branch protection or permissions change, or a workflow step failure that prevented the snapshot from being committed and pushed to the GitHub Pages branch.

Less likely but possible: The GitHub Actions workflow ran and completed but failed to commit or push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch (e.g., due to a permissions error or a git conflict), leaving the previously published file in place.

Less likely: A GitHub Pages CDN caching anomaly is serving a stale version of status.json even though a newer file was published. This is less likely because snapshotAgeMinutes=717 is a very large value inconsistent with a short-lived cache staleness.

Least likely: The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is computing age incorrectly. This is unlikely because the value of 717 is internally consistent with a workflow that has not run for approximately 12 hours.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check that calls POST /api/agents received HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-runtime probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), the probe never progressed to the runtime or chat stages, leaving all five required evidence fields absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=717, max=300)
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 717 minutes old, which is 2.39x the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to any broader website or infrastructure outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 717 minutes (approximately 12 hours). The expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot's source field confirms it is produced by github-actions, meaning the upstream workflow — not the eval runner or the website serving layer — is the component that has stalled or failed. This is an eval-detected operational gap in the snapshot publishing pipeline, not a user-facing website outage.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 717' — the sole violated assertion, confirmed by the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs lines 2168-2170, source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=717, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is structurally valid and was produced by github-actions but is stale (evidence id: failed-check.evidence).

expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 (source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:474-482).

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 and valid app shells, ruling out a shared website or CDN failure (evidence ids: sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages).

source.check-config.published-observability-snapshot: the check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational', staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry stale threshold (360 min) is more lenient than the contract assertion threshold (300 min), confirming the contract is the binding freshness gate (evidence id: source.check-config.published-observability-snapshot).
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot has not completed a successful run in over 717 minutes. This could be due to a workflow being disabled, a scheduling gap, a runner quota exhaustion, a branch protection or permissions change, or a workflow step failure that prevented the snapshot from being committed and pushed to the GitHub Pages branch.

Less likely but possible: The GitHub Actions workflow ran and completed but failed to commit or push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch (e.g., due to a permissions error or a git conflict), leaving the previously published file in place.

Less likely: A GitHub Pages CDN caching anomaly is serving a stale version of status.json even though a newer file was published. This is less likely because snapshotAgeMinutes=717 is a very large value inconsistent with a short-lived cache staleness.

Least likely: The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is computing age incorrectly. This is unlikely because the value of 717 is internally consistent with a workflow that has not run for approximately 12 hours.
